title: Biafada people - Wikipedia
text: The Biafada speak the Biafada language, which belongs to the Niger-Congo languages family. Like most West Africans, the Biafada are farmers. The staple crops for these people are cassava and rice.

title: Biafada people of Guinea-Bissau, Senegal and Gambia
text: Jun 9, 2026 · The Biafada language (also called Beafada, Ganjoola, or Bidyola) belongs to the Niger-Congo language family, specifically the North Atlantic branch. This classification places their language in structural kinship with neighbouring languages such as Balanta, Manjak, and Diola (also Jola/Joola) and, to a lesser extent, Fula.

title: Biafada language — Grokipedia
text: The Biafada language, a member of the Atlantic branch of Niger-Congo, features a consonant inventory comprising 31 consonant phones, with approximately 25 phonemes when treating prenasalized stops and affricates as unitary segments, alongside a small set of allophonic variants.
